title: OrionBridge x Redwood - Partner Intro & Discovery
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and OrionBridge to explore reseller/integration opportunities, technical compatibility (GPU fleet, networking, VPC/private deployments), and go-to-market motions. Discussed performance benchmarks, model variants, KMS and audit needs, potential pilot, and next steps to share security docs and run a small benchmark on OrionBridge A100/Tesla fleet.

Technical compatibility: GPU types, VPC/private deploy, networking and egress
Benchmarks: latency/cost tests, model variants, quantization

transcript:
Header: 2026-07-29 | 14:00 - 14:48 UTC | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Diego Ramirez (Redwood Partnerships); Liam O'Neill (OrionBridge Head of Partnerships), Dr. Sara Mostafa (OrionBridge CTO), Maya Lin (Product), Ethan Park (Infra Lead)

00:00 Liam: Hey everybody, thanks for joining, appreciate you fitting us in today. We are excited to learn how Redwood might plug into our offerings.
00:15 Alex: Thanks Liam, yeah, appreciate you folks making time. Quick round robin - I'm Alex, AE, Priya is our solutions engineer, Diego is on partnerships.
00:25 Sara: Hi, Sara here. We'll mostly be talking about integration and what level of partnership makes sense.
00:40 Priya: Great, quick agenda \u2014 intro, technical compatibility, partnership models, next steps, does that align?
00:55 Liam: Yes that works. Quick background on OrionBridge \u2014 we provide managed GPU clusters across multiple regions, focus on enterprise-friendly networking and marketplace for ISV integrations. We recently added A100 and H100 instances and some custom NVLink configs.
01:20 Diego: Nice, that aligns a lot with what our customers ask for. Do you primarily sell as a cloud provider or as a channel partner/reseller?
01:35 Liam: Both. We operate as a cloud vendor but also run a marketplace where partners can list managed services. Looking for integrations that can be offered as "Redwood on OrionBridge" and also technical partnerships for private deployments.
01:55 Maya: From product perspective we want to understand what kind of packaging you expect \u2014 a managed SaaS integration vs a self-managed image on our infra.
02:10 Alex: Typical options: 1) Redwood-hosted API running on our infra (we manage the control plane), 2) Dedicated/reserved capacity on OrionBridge for Redwood Dedicated customers, 3) Private deployment where customer runs Redwood runtime in their VPC or on-prem. We can support marketplace images as well.
02:35 Ethan: So if we were to host Redwood Dedicated on our GPU pools, what are the networking needs? Ports, egress, private link?
02:50 Priya: Good question \u2014 for Dedicated we need control-plane connectivity to Redwood for billing/console, but inference traffic can stay in your VPC. We support AWS VPC peering, PrivateLink, and in some private cases an air-gapped option where the customer controls the control plane. For the runtime you typically need outbound to our control plane for metrics and rollouts; we can run with restricted egress for pilot.
03:20 Sara: KMS and encryption? Our customers require KMS/HSM integration and key separation.
03:32 Alex: We integrate with customer KMS, and for Private we can support their KMS/HSM. For Dedicated we offer encryption at rest for KV cache and model artifacts, and you can bring your own keys. We'll share SOC2/ISO docs as well.
03:50 Liam: Perfect. Pricing model question \u2014 do you expect OrionBridge to resell or earn referral fees on Hosted usage?
04:05 Diego: We can be flexible \u2014 revenue share on hosted API, discounted reserved capacity MSRP for Dedicated, or a marketplace listing fee. We typically start with a referral/reseller pilot to validate demand.
04:25 Maya: For customers asking about latency and cost, we need benchmark numbers. How do you usually run these?
04:40 Priya: We run a small benchmark matrix \u2014 a couple of models (open Llama variants, Llama2-style, and one larger MPT/Redwood-verified model), sequence lengths at 32/128/512, and measure p50/p95 latency and tokens/sec. Also measure cost-per-token on various quantization profiles. We provide a runbook and scripts.
05:15 Ethan: What GPUs do you prefer? A100, H100, anything else? Also driver/runtime like CUDA/cuDNN versions?
05:30 Priya: We support A100 and H100 and have optimizations per architecture. Driver matrix we can work with but prefer relatively recent CUDA 11/12 stacks. We'll need the CPU and NIC specs too for multi-GPU cases.
05:50 Liam: Sounds doable. We'll share our fleet inventory.
06:05 Sara: Any concerns with KV cache and statefulness in a multi-tenant environment?
06:20 Priya: KV cache is local to the runtime instance; we recommend pinned instances for workloads needing cache. For multi-tenant we either shard by customer or use dedicated pools. We'll talk about autoscaling and cache warm-up strategies in the deep-dive.
06:45 Liam: On compliance \u2014 clients often ask for audit logs and SSO/SAML for access.
06:55 Alex: Yep, we provide role-based access control, SAML SSO integrations, and detailed audit logs per request and per model route. For enterprise we can retain logs longer as an add-on.
07:15 Maya: How often do you push model updates? Customers worry about drift/regressions.
07:25 Priya: We provide model version pinning and rollout controls \u2014 canary rollouts, A/B testing, and automatic fallback. We pair that with eval hooks so you can tie regressions to prompts and alert.
07:45 Ethan: From infra operations, we care about orchestration \u2014 how the runtime schedules across your fleet. Do you rely on Kubernetes?
08:00 Priya: Our runtime can run on Kubernetes, but many customers use a lightweight supervisor we provide that handles batching and kernel selection. On OrionBridge we can either deploy into k8s or run our supervisor directly on the nodes depending on preference.
08:25 Liam: Any known gotchas with NVLink or multi-GPU sharding?
08:35 Priya: Multi-GPU for large models needs careful kv cache and sharding logic. NVLink helps for model parallel setups; we have recommended configs. We'll share known best-practices in the doc pack.
08:50 Alex: Quick pause \u2014 mentioned earlier you run a marketplace, is your expectation to have a managed listing where customers can spin up Redwood instances in one click?
09:05 Liam: Ideally yes, marketplace listing with a one-click deploy or a managed service offering. Also open to reseller where we handle billing.
09:20 Diego: For marketplace flows we typically provide a deployable image or terraform module and Redwood provides the runtime image and docs. For managed flows we coordinate SSO and entitlement bridging.
09:35 Sara: Regarding data residency \u2014 some customers require EU-only hosting. Do you have multiple regions?
09:45 Liam: Yes EU, NA, and APAC regions. We'll note region-specific capacity constraints though.
09:55 Priya: For regionally restricted data we recommend Private deployment or a Dedicated pool pinned to the region.
10:10 Maya: Can we do a short technical demo or POC to validate perf?
10:20 Alex: Absolutely \u2014 pilot typically includes a small reserved pool on your infra, a benchmark run, and a commercial pilot.
10:30 Ethan: For the pilot we can allocate a handful of A100 nodes for a couple of days. What's the minimal setup you need?
10:40 Priya: For a basic benchmark: 4 x A100 40GB nodes, standardized driver stack, and a test VPC with ~100 Mbps egress to Redwood control-plane if needed. We'll provide an apron script and docker image.
11:00 Liam: We'll check availability but that sounds reasonable.
11:10 Diego: On GTM \u2014 Redwood has developer documentation, quickstarts, and example templates we can list. We can do joint webinars and co-marketing once pilot shows traction.
11:30 Maya: How do you handle support and runbooks for partners?
11:40 Alex: We offer partner enablement: a technical onboarding packet, a named partner success manager for first 90 days, and priority engineering support for pilots.
11:55 Sara: Are there any blockers from our side for compliance when we host Redwood?
12:05 Priya: Nothing major; we'll need to review SOC2 docs, do a quick security questionnaire, and ensure KMS integration flow is clear. We can run an NDA if needed.
12:25 Liam: Let's talk timelines \u2014 we have a few prospects asking for a "Redwood on OrionBridge" offer within 6-8 weeks. Is that realistic?
12:40 Alex: For a pilot and marketplace listing yes \u2014 6-8 weeks for a minimal proof, longer for full GTM.
13:00 Ethan: Ok we'll map out resource windows.
13:10 Priya: We'll share a benchmark plan and scripts \u2014 can we target to run the benchmark by the week of Aug 3rd?
13:20 Ethan: Yes, aiming for that.
13:30 Alex: Next steps recap \u2014 we'll send the partner one-pager, security deck, and benchmark runbook. Ethan will share fleet specs and availability. Priya and Ethan to schedule the infra deep-dive.
13:50 Liam: Great. Any last questions?
14:00 Maya: One small note \u2014 some of our enterprise customers want an option for on-prem appliance. Do you support air-gapped installs?
14:10 Priya: Yes, we have an on-prem/private deployment option that can be air-gapped; it requires more ops support but it's supported.
14:25 Diego: We'll put together a partner plan doc and propose initial commercial terms after the benchmark.
14:40 Alex: Thanks everyone \u2014 we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites.
14:48 End of recording.

Notes on transcript quality: Some technical terms were auto-transcribed imperfectly (e.g., NVLink sometimes appears as "N V link", KV cache as "K V cash"). Occasional speaker mislabels around 06:00-07:00 where AE and SE overlap. Refer to action items for definitive owners.
